facts.text: The author (26F) has been with her 30F girlfriend for just over a year, and they live together.

The author and a 27F friend have been close since school and university; five years ago the author had unreciprocated romantic feelings, they drifted apart, but mended the friendship recently and remain close.
The author and the friend planned a skating trip this year, having previously taken and enjoyed a similar trip in university.
They invited others, including the girlfriend, who declined to go.
At the girlfriend’s request, the trip date was moved to a weekend when she would be out of town, and both the author and the friend rearranged plans to accommodate this.
A third friend backed out, leaving it a two-person trip, and everything is already booked and paid.
The author did not immediately tell her girlfriend that the third friend had backed out.
When told it would just be two people, the girlfriend demanded the author cancel and refused to allow the trip.
The girlfriend claimed the trip would be a two-night, three-day date, said it betrayed her trust, and called it akin to cheating.
The girlfriend set rules that the author must not initiate contact with the friend, must not hang out with her privately, and should distance herself from the friendship.
The author refused to cancel and told the girlfriend they should both reconsider the relationship, citing the girlfriend’s controlling behavior and lack of trust.
The girlfriend removed the author from chat apps, said she would not consider breaking up, and told the author to decide alone and email the result.
The author states the girlfriend had not previously shown insecurities about this friend.
The author and the friend still intend to go on the trip.
The author asserts her relationship with the friend is now purely platonic and she does not foresee anything romantic developing.
